error_unreachable: The API at {api} did not answer this app. It answers the admin only when its ADMIN_ORIGIN is {origin}, exactly as written here. If it is, the API may be stopped.
auth_failed: That did not work. Try again.
not_operator_title: This account has nothing to read here
not_operator_write: It says which account it found. Run it again with --write to make that account an operator, then reload this page.
copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.
developers_empty: No developer account yet. Create one for whoever consumes the API, then make it a key.
developer_contact_hint: How you reach whoever holds the keys. Yours to leave out.
developer_limit_hint: Shared by the account's keys. Leave it empty for no limit.
developer_limit_invalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 999,999, or nothing.
developer_delete_body: Its keys stop working at once, and its keys and their counts are deleted. To stop an account and keep its history, suspend it instead.
orphan_keys_body: An earlier version of the instance made these keys. They work without a limit. Revoke them, and make new ones for a developer account.
key_new_body: For {developer}. It reads the data everyone shares, and nothing of an account.
key_name_hint: The program that will hold it, such as "tide clock".
key_made_body: This is the only time "{name}" is shown: the instance keeps its hash, not the key.
key_revoke_body: The key stops working at once, and never works again.
usage_chart_label: Calls from {start} to {end}, answered and not answered
usage_empty: No call in this span of time.
usage_empty_keys: No call with a key in this span of time.
usage_empty_mcp: No call by the MCP server in this span of time.
via_link: Readers of a shared list, by its link
via_visitor: Visitors of the web app, with no account
outcome_invalid_hint: The request was wrong: something missing, or something that does not exist.
outcome_refused_hint: The caller was not accepted: no name, a key that does not work, or no right to this.
outcome_limited_hint: The developer account had made its calls for the hour.
outcome_failed_hint: The instance failed: a fault of its own, or a provider that did not answer.
accounts_search: Search a name, a username or an address
account_username_remove_body: What the account wrote in a guide stays, and names nobody. The account chooses another username before it contributes again.
action_developer_created_with: Created the account, with {limit} calls an hour
action_limit: Changed the calls an hour from {from} to {to}
account_session_renewed_note: A session is renewed about once a day while it is used.
account_sign_out_body: Every device signed in to this account will have to sign in again. It keeps nobody out: the account can sign in at once.
account_sign_out_own_body: Every device signed in to your account will have to sign in again, this one too.
account_suspend_body: Its sessions are closed and it cannot sign in until you let it in again. What it owns stays, and what it shared stays visible.
account_operator_note: An operator is not suspended. Take the account's operator rights away first, with the command that gave them.
account_history_empty: Nothing was done to this account.
action_unknown: Did something this admin has no words for yet: {action}
command_palette_placeholder: Search pages, actions and developer accounts
shortcuts_description: Select a shortcut, then press the new keys. Backspace turns it off. They belong to this browser.
shortcuts_incomplete: Add a key to the combination.
mail_off_note: The instance sends no mail, and checks no account's address.
mail_today: Mails counted today, sent or only tried, through {via}
instance_web_origin: Web app, as the API holds it
instance_admin_site: Admin's site, as the API holds it
instance_processes: Worker processes of the last day
worker_never_seen: No worker was seen in the last day.
usage_not_written: Nothing written since the API started
usage_lost: {count} calls counted and not written since the API started
jobs_empty: No job yet. The worker lists its jobs when it starts: none has started on this database with a version that does.
failure_provider_silent: The provider at {host} did not answer.
failure_format: The provider's answer had changed shape.
failure_database: The database refused what the job wrote.
failure_expired: The run was not over when its time was up.
failure_stopped: The worker stopped before the run was over.
failure_other: The job failed for another reason. The worker's log says which.
forecasts_note: The instance counts each request it sends to its forecast provider, and stays under what the provider's free tier allows. Past a limit it asks nothing: a forecast that is kept answers for a day, and says it is an older one.
forecast_calls_people: Today, for the people who look
forecast_cells_note: One for each point that was asked for, to the nearest 0.05°, fetched again after two hours.
count_stale: {count} left for want of a fresh forecast
providers_note: A reading leaves the map after six hours. A provider that publishes a day late has none under six hours and works as it should: its job says how it runs.
processes_note: One process is the rule. Two overlap for a moment during a deployment. Several that started minutes apart and never were ready are a worker that fails to start.
not_operator_member: To read the keys and the calls of a developer account here, ask an operator of the instance to add this account to its members. This identifier tells them which account is yours:
not_operator_host: If you host this instance, an operator is named from the server, with this command:
console_palette_placeholder: Search a developer account or a preference
console_read_only: You read this developer account. An operator of the instance makes its keys and sets its limit.
console_suspended_note: An operator of the instance suspended this developer account: none of its keys works.
console_missing_title: This developer account does not exist, or this account is not one of its members
members_hint: A member signs in to this admin and reads this account's limit, its keys by name and their calls. It changes nothing, and never sees a key, the contact or the note.
members_empty: No member. Only the operators read this account.
member_add_body: Choose the account of whoever holds the keys. An address says nothing of who holds an account, checked or not: choose the one you know to be theirs, and ask them for its identifier when in doubt.
member_unchecked_note: Its address was never checked: anyone may have signed up with it.
member_suspended_note: It is suspended, and reads nothing until it is let in again.
member_remove_body: It reads nothing of this developer account from its next call.
member_remove_last_body: It reads nothing of this developer account from its next call. Only the operators will read it then.
action_member_added_to: Added it to the members of {developer}
action_member_removed_from: Removed it from the members of {developer}
moderation_intro: Spots their owners ask to make public. Accept one that is known to all: it joins the catalogue of surf breaks, under the ODbL and with no account named. Refuse a spot that few people know, and one the catalogue already has.
moderation_empty: No spot waits for an answer.
moderation_others_none: No other account has a spot within 150 m
moderation_others_one: One other account has a spot of its own within 150 m
moderation_others_some: {count} other accounts have a spot of their own within 150 m
moderation_accept_body: Its name, its point and what its owner says of it join the catalogue, for everyone. The owner's later changes will not change it.
moderation_refuse_body: The spot stays private. Its owner reads the reason, and may ask again.
reviews_intro: What accounts wrote of the breaks, line by line. Accept what is right: the guide then says it, under its author’s username. Refuse what is wrong, with a reason its author reads.
reviews_empty_pending: No contribution waits to be read.
reviews_empty_shown: No contribution waits to be confirmed.
reviews_break_gone: A break that left the catalogue
reviews_refuse_body: Its author reads the reason. A line that said it says again what it said before.
action_contribution_accepted: Confirmed a contribution to a guide
action_contribution_refused: Refused a contribution to a guide
action_contribution_kept: Kept a contested contribution to a guide
action_spot_refused: Refused to make a spot public
visitors_open_note: Anyone reads the map without an account.
visitors_closed_note: Closed {ago}. The app asks for an account.
visitors_busy_note: Closed by itself: {count} forecast requests were sent today for the people who look. The app asks for an account until midnight UTC.
visitors_auto_note: Closes by itself at {count} forecast requests in a day, until midnight UTC.
visitors_close_body: Whoever has no account reads that a lot of people are here, and is asked to sign in or to create one. Accounts, keys and shared lists work as before.
visitors_open_body: Anyone reads the map, the buoys and the forecasts without an account. Saving a spot or setting an alert still takes one.
catalogue_marker: The point being placed. Drag it, or press the map where it goes.
catalogue_search: Find a break by its name
catalogue_pick: Press a break on the map, or find it by its name.
catalogue_close_none: No two breaks are that close.
catalogue_point_hint: Drag the marker, or press the map where the break is.
catalogue_offshore_hint: In degrees, clockwise from north. Leave it empty when nobody knows.
catalogue_size_hint: The height of the wave faces, in meters. Leave a bound empty when nobody gives one.
catalogue_fault_size: Each bound is a number of meters from 0 to {most}, the smallest no larger than the largest.
catalogue_confirmed: The guide shows {words}, which an account wrote and others confirmed.
catalogue_description_hint: A few sentences, in your own words. Anyone reads them in the break's guide.
catalogue_description_own: A few sentences, in your own words: the list's texts are for you to read, not to copy.
catalogue_fault_point: A latitude from -90 to 90 and a longitude from -180 to 180.
catalogue_delete_used: Accounts use this break: merge it into another one instead.
catalogue_delete_confirm_body: The break leaves the catalogue, and adding its list again does not bring it back. A candidate that went into it waits to be decided again.
catalogue_merge_body: One stays, and everything that used the other uses it. Choose what it keeps where the two differ.
catalogue_merge_moves: The spots ({spots}), lists ({lists}) and sessions ({sessions}) of {name} move to the break that stays.
catalogue_merge_pick: Choose the break to merge into, on the map or in the list.
catalogue_alike: {count} other fields are the same on both.
catalogue_proposal_merge: Proposed: a break of the catalogue
action_candidate_reopened: Put candidate {ref} back in the queue
catalogue_merge_confirmed: The guide shows what accounts confirmed, whatever the merge keeps: {lines}.
